Total fell 234.5 -> 226.5 open to close (slate data), consistent with Indiana losing more offense after the open. Helps Atlanta.

Covers odds page lists Atlanta -10.5 with moneylines around -429 / +370 at the close (Covers matchup odds, archived pre-game). Confirms the move. Helps Atlanta at -4.5.
Andrew Nembhard averaging 21 points on 17 shots over his last three with a 34.6% usage rate (Covers, Nov 2, 2026) -- Indiana's offense runs through one healthy guard. Slightly helps Atlanta.
games.reasoning: What decided it is the slate number versus the market: Atlanta -4.5 against a close of -10.5, after a 3-point move from the open on news the market saw after the slate line was set. Per LESSONS I treat the moved number as fair rather than fading it, which projects Atlanta by about 9 and clears the bar even shaded halfway to the line. The [angle] is a depleted Indiana on the second night of a back-to-back after a home loss to the 1-5 Nets. It would have been a pass if the line had stayed near 5.5, or if the move had been toward Indiana.

The [angle] that kept it from being a lean is the Nets on the second night of a back-to-back with Mikel Brown Jr. unconfirmed, which offsets the Knicks' slow, inefficient offense. Forced side: Brooklyn, on the Knicks never winning by more than 14 at a slow pace and the tentative lesson against laying big numbers with a reshuffled early favorite.
